title: Per-component enlargement lemmas assemble the greedy chain for equation 1729 not implying 817
intent: Reduce the existence of a magma satisfying equation 1729 but not 817 to a greedy chain over a sum-indexed task beta = N + N + (N x N), seeded by TrivialPartialSolution and turned into a magma by use_chain, with each component of the index closed by its own enlargement lemma.

parent.name: not_817
parent.statement: theorem not_817 : ∃ (G: Type) (_: Magma G), Equation1729 G ∧ ¬ Equation817 G

children.name: use_chain
children.statement: lemma use_chain {sols : Set PartialSolution} (hchain: IsChain (fun (sol1 sol2 : PartialSolution) => sol1 ≤ sol2) sols ) (hnon: Nonempty sols) (htotal_L₀' : ∀ x : N, ∃ sol ∈ sols, x ∈ sol.Dom_L₀') (htotal_S' : ∀ x : N, ∃ sol ∈ sols, x ∈ sol.Dom_S') (htotal_op : ∀ (x y : N), ∃ sol ∈ sols, (x,y) ∈ sol.Dom_op) : ∃ (G: Type) (_: Magma G), Equation1729 G ∧ ¬ Equation817 G
children.closed_by: filter limit over `Filter.atTop` on `sols`, defining S', op, L₀' by `Set.choose`, then `apply @reduce_to_new_axioms S' L₀' op` (SmallMagma.lean:431), each axiom discharged by `filter_upwards` over the partial-solution axiom fields

children.name: enlarge_L₀'
children.statement: lemma enlarge_L₀' (sol : PartialSolution) (x : N)  : ∃ sol', sol ≤ sol' ∧ x ∈ fill sol'.Predom_L₀' ∧ sol.Dom_S' = sol'.Dom_S'
children.closed_by: `by_cases hx : x ∈ sol.Dom_L₀'`; else `set sol' := enlarge_L₀'_by hx hed (gen_fresh_not_rel_extra ...) hcol1 hcol2` after proving the two non-collision facts hcol1/hcol2, then closes with `enlarge_L₀'_extends` (line 558)

children.name: enlarge_S'
children.statement:
lemma enlarge_S' (sol : PartialSolution) (x : N) :
    ∃ sol', sol ≤ sol' ∧ x ∈ sol'.Dom_S'
children.closed_by: `apply WellFoundedLT.induction x`; both the base (z = 1) and step cases call `enlarge_S'_induction` (lines 2049 and 2053)

children.name: enlarge_op
children.statement: lemma enlarge_op (sol : PartialSolution) (x y :N) : ∃ sol', sol ≤ sol' ∧ (x,y) ∈ sol'.Dom_op
children.closed_by: three `wlog`'s (x ∈ Dom_S', y ∈ Dom_S', w ∈ Dom_L₀') that call `enlarge_S'` and `enlarge_L₀'`, then `by_cases` on x = y, x = R' a y, else; each case builds a new PartialSolution extending `Dom_op` by one entry

children.name: TrivialPartialSolution
children.statement: def TrivialPartialSolution : PartialSolution := { L₀' := fun _ ↦ 1, op := fun _ ↦ fun _ ↦ Sum.inl 0, S' := fun _ ↦ 0, I := Finset.empty, Predom_L₀' := Finset.empty, Dom_op := Finset.empty, Dom_S' := Finset.empty, ... }
children.closed_by: each of the ten `axiom_*` fields is closed by `contrapose! h; exact Finset.notMem_empty _`, since every domain field is `Finset.empty`

applicability.goal_shape: An existence goal ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Magma G), P G ∧ ¬ Q G whose intended model is the limit of a chain of finite partial solutions, each step governed by a totality condition indexed by a finite sum type (here N ⊕ N ⊕ (N × N)).
applicability.use_when: the construction is a greedy/back-and-forth limit whose single-step move is a family of near-identical enlargement lemmas, one per component of the index type, so the glue is a dispatch over that index; a generic chain combinator (exists_greedy_chain) and a chain-to-magma lemma (use_chain) already exist.
applicability.avoid_when: the components need genuinely different enlargement arguments that do not share one PartialSolution structure (then they are not one family); the limit combinator is not available, so the glue itself would carry real work; or there are many components, where a generated or folded form beats one hand-written lemma per component.

The glue dispatches over the three components of β = N ⊕ N ⊕ (N × N) (the `match b with` at lines 32-43), one enlargement lemma per component, and the whole main proof is 29 lines (lines 15-43).

consequences: Each constructor of the index sum β = N ⊕ N ⊕ (N × N) is a separate closure obligation on the greedy chain: Sum.inl x, Sum.inr (Sum.inl x), Sum.inr (Sum.inr (x,y)). The glue must (a) instantiate exists_greedy_chain with a task whose three components match use_chain's three totality hypotheses, (b) seed it nonempty with TrivialPartialSolution, and (c) cover every constructor in the match (exhaustiveness is Lean's coverage check on `match b with`, not a separate lemma). The failure mode is a component whose enlargement lemma does not preserve the other components' domains: enlarge_L₀' therefore returns `sol.Dom_S' = sol'.Dom_S'` explicitly, and enlarge_op wlogs its prerequisites via enlarge_S'/enlarge_L₀' before extending Dom_op.
